title: Aqueous based reflux method for green synthesis of nanostructures: Application in CZTS synthesis
author: Aditha, Kurdekar, et al.

steps.title: Assemble reflux apparatus
steps.instruction: Set up a round‑bottom flask fitted with a Liebig or Vigreux condenser; circulate chilled water through the condenser jacket and, if higher temperature is required, place the flask in an oil or sand bath; use a magnetic stirrer for uniform heating.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous precursor solutions
steps.instruction: Make separate aqueous solutions of (i) 1 M CuCl₂, (ii) 0.5 M ZnCl₂, and (iii) 0.5 M SnCl₂·2H₂O; also prepare a 2 M aqueous solution of thio‑urea.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve CuCl₂ in water to obtain 1 M concentration.
Dissolve ZnCl₂ in water to obtain 0.5 M concentration.
Dissolve SnCl₂·2H₂O in water to obtain 0.5 M concentration.
Dissolve thio‑urea in water to obtain 2 M concentration.

steps.title: Mix thio‑urea with tin chloride
steps.instruction: Transfer the 2 M thio‑urea solution into the reflux flask, add the 0.5 M SnCl₂ solution, and stir until the mixture becomes clear.

steps.title: Add copper and zinc solutions
steps.instruction: Add the 1 M CuCl₂ solution and the 0.5 M ZnCl₂ solution to the flask simultaneously while stirring.

steps.title: Reflux reaction mixture
steps.instruction: Heat the mixture to the boiling point of the solvent and maintain reflux for 8 h; the temperature is governed by the solvent’s boiling point.

steps.title: Cool reaction to room temperature
steps.instruction: Allow the refluxed mixture to cool gradually to ambient temperature.

steps.title: Filter and wash product
steps.instruction: Filter the resulting solid, then wash the cake repeatedly with distilled water and ethanol (several times).

steps.title: Dry powder under vacuum
steps.instruction: Place the washed solid in a vacuum oven and dry until a dry powder is obtained.

steps.title: Perform X‑ray diffraction analysis
steps.instruction: Collect XRD patterns using a Panalytical diffractometer with Cu Kα radiation (λ = 1.5406 Å) and a step size of 2°/min; note peaks at 2θ = 28.54°, 33.76°, 47.5°, 56.24° corresponding to kesterite CZTS (JCPDS #26‑0575).

steps.title: Calculate crystallite size (Scherrer)
steps.instruction: Use the Scherrer formula D = 0.9 λ β / cos θ (λ = 1.5406 Å) on the XRD peaks to obtain an average crystallite size of 2.5 nm.

steps.title: Acquire Raman spectrum
steps.instruction: Record Raman spectra with a Horiba iHR 550 spectrophotometer using a 532 nm laser; identify CZTS peaks at 307 cm⁻¹ and 339 cm⁻¹.
